candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: identifyingTest
candidates.comment: An identifying test relation between a medical sign and a medical test that can detect it. Also called diagnostic test, detection test, test for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying test of a blood panel.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying test.", "This sign requires an identifying test.". Distinct from identifyingExam, which refers to a physical examination.

candidates.label: identifyingExam
candidates.comment: An identifying exam relation between a medical sign and a physical examination that can detect it. Also called diagnostic exam, detection exam, exam for sign. Examples: "A medical sign has an identifying exam of a neurological check.", "The symptom is detected by an identifying exam.", "This sign requires an identifying exam."

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: gettingTestedInfo
candidates.comment: A getting tested info relation between a special announcement and information regarding testing for a medical condition. Also called: testing information, diagnostic details, screening guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement" getting tested info "CDC Testing Guidelines", "Flu Season Alert" getting tested info "Local Clinic Testing Sites", "Public Health Notice" getting tested info "Symptoms and Testing Advice".

candidates.label: checkinTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a lodging business or reservation, indicating the earliest time for check-in. Also called "arrival time", "earliest check-in", "check-in starts". Examples: "Hotel lodging business checkinTime '15:00'", "Flight reservation checkinTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00'". Distinct from checkoutTime, which specifies the latest time for departure.

candidates.label: jobImmediateStart
candidates.comment: An employment timing relation indicating whether a job position is available for an immediate start. Also called immediate start, urgent hire, start now, ready to begin. Examples: A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'true'. A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'false'. This position has jobImmediateStart as 'true' for qualified candidates. Distinct from jobStartDate, which specifies a particular date.

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. candidates.label: usesDevice

candidates.label: employee

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

chosen_property.label: publishedIn
chosen_property.definition: To be published in a particular publication
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: publicationType
candidates.comment: A publication type relation between a medical scholarly article and its classification according to a catalog like MeSH. Also called article type, MeSH type. Examples: "A medical article has a publication type 'Review'.", "A research paper has a publication type 'Clinical Trial'.", "A case study has a publication type 'Case Report'."

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: publishingPrinciples
candidates.comment: A publishing principles relation between a creative work, organization, or person and the document outlining their editorial and ethical guidelines as a publisher. Also called editorial guidelines, ethics policy, publishing policy. Examples: "A news organization has publishing principles outlined on its website.", "A research journal adheres to specific publishing principles.", "A blogger follows certain publishing principles for their content."

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: publisherImprint
candidates.comment: A publisher imprint relation between a creative work and the specific publishing division or imprint responsible for its release. Also called imprint of, published under imprint. Examples: "A comic book has a publisher imprint 'Vertigo Comics'.", "A novel has a publisher imprint 'Vintage Books'.", "A children's book has a publisher imprint 'Puffin Books'."

candidates.label: bookEdition
candidates.comment: A textual description of the edition of a book. Also called: edition number, publication edition. Examples: "Book 'The Lord of the Rings' bookEdition 'First Edition'", "Book 'Textbook' bookEdition '2nd Edition'."

chosen_property.label: toldTo
chosen_property.definition: To inform or communicate something to someone
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

chosen_property.label: investigates
chosen_property.definition: To conduct an inquiry or examination into something
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview
candidates.comment: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: itemReviewed
candidates.comment: A review subject relation between an aggregate rating or review and the entity that is being evaluated or rated. Also called reviewed item, rated item, subject of review, evaluated entity. Examples: A review has an itemReviewed of 'Restaurant X'. An aggregate rating has an itemReviewed of 'Movie Y'. A product review has an itemReviewed of 'Smartphone Z'. Distinct from itemOffered, which is the subject of an offer or demand.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

chosen_property.label: isPartOf
chosen_property.definition: To be a component or member of something
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: partOfSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode or clip and the creative work season it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a season. A clip from a show is part of a season. The season finale is part of a season.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: partOfEpisode
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a clip and the episode it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is featured in, belongs to, is from. Examples: A highlight reel is part of an episode. A deleted scene is part of an episode. A short preview is part of an episode.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.

chosen_property.label: launchedFrom
chosen_property.definition: To be launched or started from a particular location
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: applicationStartDate
candidates.comment: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: departureAirport
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a flight and the airport from which it originates. Also called: origin airport, departure airfield, flight departure point. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure airport "London Heathrow Airport", "Flight UA123" departure airport "San Francisco International Airport". Distinct from arrivalAirport, which is the destination airport.

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: departurePlatform
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a train trip and the platform from which it departs. Also called: platform number, train platform, departure track. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure platform "Platform 5", "Commuter Train" departure platform "Track 3". Distinct from arrivalPlatform, which is the arrival platform.

candidates.label: targetPlatform
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of platform for which an API reference is intended, such as phone or desktop. Also called "platform type", "development platform", "operating system target", "device target". Examples: "The API reference has targetPlatform iOS", "The software's targetPlatform is Windows Desktop", "This API is designed for targetPlatform Android."

chosen_property.label: carriedBy
chosen_property.definition: To be transported or conveyed by something
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: holdingArchive
candidates.comment: A holding archive relation between an archive component and the archive organization that maintains it. Also called maintained by, kept by, archive holder. Examples: "An archive component has a holding archive 'National Archives'.", "The document is part of a holding archive.", "This record is held by a specific holding archive."

candidates.label: roofLoad
candidates.comment: The maximum permissible weight that can be carried on the roof of a vehicle, including cargo and any installations. Also called roof capacity, maximum roof weight, roof rack load limit. Examples: `SUV Model X` roofLoad `75 kg`, `Sedan Model Y` roofLoad `50 kg`, `Van Model Z` roofLoad `100 kg`. Distinct from `cargoVolume`, which refers to the internal cargo space.

candidates.label: itemShipped
candidates.comment: A shipment content relation between a parcel delivery and the product(s) being transported. Also called shipped product, contents of shipment, parcel contents, delivered item. Examples: A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'a book'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'clothing items'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'electronic device'.

candidates.label: bloodSupply
candidates.comment: A blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to a muscle. Also called: muscle blood flow, arterial supply. Examples: "Muscle 'Bicep' bloodSupply 'Brachial Artery'", "Muscle 'Heart' bloodSupply 'Coronary Arteries'."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: cargoVolume
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement of the available volume for cargo or luggage in a vehicle. Also called "trunk volume", "luggage capacity", "storage volume". Examples: "Car vehicle cargoVolume 400 LTR", "Truck vehicle cargoVolume 100 FTQ".

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: carrier
candidates.comment: A provider relation between a flight or parcel delivery and the organization that provides the service. Also called "provider", "airline", "delivery service". Examples: "Flight from London to NYC carrier British Airways", "Parcel delivery carrier FedEx".

chosen_property.label: owner
chosen_property.justification: Inverse of owner property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: copyrightHolder
candidates.comment: A legal ownership relation between a creative work and the person or organization holding its copyright. Also called: copyright owner, rights holder, legally owned by. Examples: "The Mona Lisa" copyright holder "The Louvre Museum", "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" copyright holder "J.K. Rowling", "Microsoft Windows" copyright holder "Microsoft Corporation".

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: landlord
candidates.comment: A property ownership relation between a rent action and the person or organization that owns and leases the real estate. Also called property owner, lessor, rental owner, proprietor. Examples: A rent action has a landlord of 'John Doe'. A rent action has a landlord of 'Property Management Inc.'. A lease agreement lists 'Sarah Smith' as the landlord. Distinct from agent, which is the general actor of an action.

candidates.label: numberOfPreviousOwners
candidates.comment: The total number of previous owners of a vehicle, including the current owner. Also called prior owners, owner history count, past owners. Examples: "Used Car A numberOfPreviousOwners 1", "Vintage Vehicle B numberOfPreviousOwners 3", "New Car C numberOfPreviousOwners 0".

candidates.label: ownershipFundingInfo
candidates.comment: Information describing the ownership structure, funding, and grants of an organization, particularly concerning editorial independence for news media. Also called funding transparency, ownership structure, financial backing details. Examples: "News Org A ownershipFundingInfo 'https://news.example.com/about/funding'", "Company B ownershipFundingInfo 'Privately held by XYZ Group.'", "Nonprofit C ownershipFundingInfo 'Funded by grants from various foundations.'". Distinct from funder, which specifically identifies the entity providing funds.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

chosen_property.label: image
chosen_property.justification: Image property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: photos
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to multiple photographs depicting it. Also called images, pictures, visual representations, gallery. Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

candidates.label: screenshot
candidates.comment: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.

candidates.label: primaryImageOfPage
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a web page to its main or most prominent image. Also called main image, featured image, hero image. Examples: A web page has a primary image of page 'logo.png'. The article page has a primary image of page 'main_illustration.jpg'. The product page's primary image of page is the 'product_hero.webp'.

candidates.label: thumbnail
candidates.comment: A smaller, preview image (thumbnail) associated with a creative work, such as an image or video. Also called "preview image", "thumbnail graphic", "miniature image", "small image". Examples: "The video has thumbnail a still frame", "The image gallery's thumbnail is a reduced version", "This creative work displays a thumbnail for quick viewing.". Distinct from image, which refers to the full-size image.

candidates.label: caption
candidates.comment: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".

candidates.label: layoutImage
candidates.comment: A visual representation relation between a floor plan and an image depicting its layout. Also called floorplan image, layout diagram, schematic image, visual layout. Examples: A floor plan has a layoutImage of 'floorplan.jpg'. A floor plan has a layoutImage of 'https://example.com/layout.png'. The apartment's floor plan includes a layoutImage. Distinct from image, which is a general image of the item, not specifically the layout.

candidates.label: diagram
candidates.comment: An illustrative relation between an anatomical structure and an image containing a diagram of it. Also called: anatomical illustration, structural diagram, visual representation. Examples: "Human Heart" diagram "Image of heart chambers and vessels", "Brain Anatomy" diagram "Diagram showing lobes and functions", "Skeletal System" diagram "Illustration of bone structure".

candidates.label: thumbnailUrl
candidates.comment: A URL pointing to a smaller, preview image (thumbnail) relevant to a creative work. Also called "thumbnail link", "preview image URL", "miniature image URL". Examples: "The video has thumbnailUrl 'http://example.com/thumb.jpg'", "The image gallery's thumbnailUrl is a link to its preview", "This creative work provides a thumbnailUrl for quick access.". Distinct from url, which is a general URL for the thing itself.

chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: studyDesign
candidates.comment: A specification of the design methodology for a medical observational study. Also called "observational study type", "research design", "study methodology". Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: trialDesign
candidates.comment: A trial design relation between a medical trial and the specific methodology or structure of the trial. Also called study design, experimental design, trial methodology. Examples: "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'RandomizedControlledTrial'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'ObservationalStudy'", "MedicalTrial trialDesign 'DoubleBlindTrial'".

candidates.label: termDuration
candidates.comment: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: termsPerYear
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating how many terms of study are offered per year within an educational or occupational program. Also called "terms offered annually", "semesters per year", "academic terms per year". Examples: "The program has termsPerYear 2", "The educational program's termsPerYear is 4 (quarters)", "This institution offers termsPerYear 3 (trimesters)."

candidates.label: inSupportOf
candidates.comment: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."

candidates.label: epidemiology
candidates.comment: An epidemiology relation between a medical condition or physical activity and the text describing the characteristics of associated patients. Also called "patient demographics", "disease characteristics", "population data". Examples: "Medical condition 'Flu' epidemiology 'Affects all ages, higher risk in elderly and young children'", "Physical activity 'Running' epidemiology 'Common among young adults, higher injury rates in beginners'", "Disease 'Diabetes' epidemiology 'Higher prevalence in certain ethnic groups'".
